senses.gloss: c. (b. h.; cmp. שָׂדַד; v. Del. Assyr. Handw. s. v. šid (d) u, p. 642) tract of land, field.
units: Shebi. I, 1, a. fr. שְׂדֵה האילן a cultivated field in which trees grow, opp. שְׂ׳ הלבן, v. לָבָן. Sifra B’ḥuck., Par. 4, ch. XI (ref. to Lev. XXVII, 21) מגיד שהש׳ קרוי לשון זכר וכ׳ this proves that sadeh is of masculine gender in the sacred (Biblical) language.
<cite ref="Mishnah Arakhin 8:1">Arakh. VIII, 1</cite> <he>המקדיש את שָׂדֵהוּ</he> if a man consecrates his field.

<cite ref="Mishnah Arakhin 7:5">Ib. VII, 5</cite> <he>הלוקח … כשְׂ׳ אחוזה</he> if a man bought a field of his father, and his father died, and after this he consecrated it, it is legally treated as an inherited field (<cite ref="Leviticus 27:16">Lev. XXVII, 16</cite>), contrad. to <he>שְׂ׳ מקנה</he> a purchased field (ib. 22); a. fr.—
<cite ref="Mishnah Ketubot 1:6">Keth. I, 6</cite>, a. e. <he>נסתחפה שדהו</he>, <he>שָׂדְךָ</he>, v. <cite ref="O00461"><he>סָחַף</he></cite>.—
<cite ref="Tosefta Shevi'it 6:21">Tosef. Shebi. VI, 21</cite> <he>ירקות סָדֶה</he> ed. Zuck. (Var. <he>ש׳</he>) vegetable growing in the field (in the Sabbatical year).—Pl. <he>שָׂדוֹת</he>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Arakhin 9:5">Arakh. IX, 5</cite> <he>כל שהוא … חוץ מן הש׳</he> whatever is within a city wall is legally the same as houses, except fields.
